entries.text: Rotating to a nitrogen-fixing legume (such as green gram, chickpea or pigeon pea) after a heavy-nutrient crop like rice, wheat or maize can help naturally restore some soil nitrogen for the next season.

Growing the same heavy-nutrient crop repeatedly on the same plot without a break crop tends to deplete specific nutrients and organic matter faster, which is why a rotation or a season of rest with compost is generally recommended.
Soil nutrient levels change season to season depending on what was grown and applied, so re-testing before the next crop gives a more accurate picture than reusing old numbers.
